key_insight: Phonon Fine-Tuning (PFT) directly supervises MLIPs on second-order derivatives by matching the model energy Hessian to DFT-computed force constants, substantially improving predicted vibrational (phonon) properties with targeted fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Standard MLIP losses (energy/forces/stress) do not guarantee correct curvature of the potential energy surface, causing large errors in vibrational spectra and derivative-dependent properties; PFT fixes this by adding explicit second-derivative supervision.
method: Compute DFT force-constant matrices via finite-displacement phonon calculations for representative structures.
Compute MLIP energy Hessians and add a Hessian-matching loss term to training, then fine-tune pretrained MLIPs to minimize curvature errors.
Validate by comparing phonon dispersion and derived thermodynamic properties before vs. after PFT to ensure improved vibrational fidelity.
impact: PFT enables MLIP users to obtain accurate phonon spectra, thermal and vibrational properties, and curvature-sensitive predictions without full retraining—improving reliability for materials modeling tasks that depend on second derivatives.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: DFT finite-displacement → force-constant matrix → Hessian loss → MLIP fine-tuning
Before/after phonon dispersion plots showing improved band frequencies and removal of spurious modes
Heatmap of Hessian (force-constant) error pre- and post-fine-tuning to visualize curvature correction
Bar chart or table summarizing improvements in phonon RMSE and downstream thermal property errors
paper_title: PFT: Phonon Fine-tuning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
paper_authors: Teddy Koker, Abhijeet Gangan, Mit Kotak, Jaime Marian, Tess Smidt
